outline.description: Introduces the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) in tabular learning, the limitations of current approaches, and an overview of the FeatLLM framework.
subtopics: The role of LLMs in reasoning and tabular learning
Current limitations: end-to-end prediction costs, fine-tuning requirements, and prompt size constraints
The FeatLLM paradigm: LLMs as feature engineers
Key benefits of FeatLLM: low inference cost, API-level access, and prompt size mitigation

outline.description: Provides foundational knowledge on few-shot learning for tabular data and explores previous methods of integrating LLMs with tabular datasets.
subtopics: Challenges and strategies in few-shot tabular learning
Unsupervised pre-training and data augmentation approaches (e.g., SubTab, VIME, SCARF, STUNT)
Transfer learning in tabular data (e.g., TransTab, TabPFN)
Language-interfaced tabular learning: data serialization and in-context learning
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques (e.g., LoRA, IA3)

outline.description: Details the core methodology of FeatLLM, covering prompt design, rule extraction, feature generation, and the downstream inference model.
subtopics: Problem formulation for tabular learning tasks
Prompt design for rule extraction
Basic information description: task, features, and serialized demonstrations
Two-step reasoning instruction: causal inference and rule deduction
Response instruction: formatting rules for automated parsing
Parsing natural language rules into executable code for feature generation
Inferring class likelihood using a non-negative weighted linear model
Ensembling with bagging: introducing randomness and overcoming prompt size limits

outline.description: Outlines the experimental design used to validate FeatLLM, including datasets, baselines, and implementation details, and discusses the primary results.
subtopics: Dataset overview: real-world, recent, and synthetic tabular datasets
Baseline methods: traditional machine learning, unlabeled data approaches, and LLM-based models
Implementation details: model configurations and hyperparameter settings
Main results: FeatLLM's performance against baselines in various few-shot regimes
Efficiency of FeatLLM compared to models requiring larger sample sizes

outline.description: Examines the inner workings of FeatLLM through ablation studies, computational cost analysis, feature quality assessment, and robustness checks.
subtopics: Ablation study: evaluating the impact of weight tuning, ensembling, descriptions, and reasoning
Training and inference time comparison across different methods
Assessing the quality and informativeness of generated features
Robustness to spurious correlations in low-shot regimes
Hyper-parameter analysis: optimizing the number of ensembles and rules

outline.chapter_title: Conclusion, Broader Impact, and Future Directions
outline.description: Summarizes the FeatLLM framework, discusses its real-world implications, and outlines potential future research avenues.
subtopics: Summary of FeatLLM's contributions to few-shot tabular learning
Broader impact: applications in data-scarce industries like finance and healthcare
Ethical considerations: societal biases and misinformation in LLM prior knowledge
Future work: scaling to larger datasets, exploring diverse feature types, and enhancing interpretability
